title: Omitting partial types: avoiding nonprincipal requirements

based_on.title: An Introduction to Model Theory
based_on.pages: 19–20 (Definition 4.1.5 and Theorem 4.1.6); PDF dated 2021-07-13; final model restricted to named elementary submodel

summary: Omit countably many nonprincipal partial types over a satisfiable, possibly incomplete theory, using actual failed requirements at every named tuple.
abstract: A partial type records requirements without answering every possible question about a tuple. When can a model avoid all tuples satisfying those requirements? If no single consistent formula forces the whole description, a countable model can avoid it. Countably many such descriptions can be avoided together, even when the original axioms leave some sentences undecided. We prove this extension of the omitting types theorem and explain two distinctions behind it: avoiding one complete description may leave solutions of the original requirements, and an incomplete theory can sometimes omit even a partial type forced by one formula.
